description: Accurate Professional Title and Role for PAs
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the need for accurate representation of Physician Associates (PAs) in regulatory language, ensuring proper nomenclature. It includes advocating for the correct use of the dual title "Physician Assistant/Physician Associate" and updating definitions to accurately reflect PAs as autonomous, licensed medical providers, rather than delegates or surrogates, excluding the specific clinical duties of PAs. The key distinction is the focus on the nomenclature and accurate portrayal of the PA profession. This matters for correct system identification and professional respect.

description: Exclusion of PAs as Delegates/Surrogates in Regulatory Language
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses concerns about language in the proposed rule that mischaracterizes Physician Associates (PAs) as delegates or surrogates. It includes advocating for the cessation of reliance on such language in studies and recommendations, ensuring PAs are viewed as autonomous providers, excluding arguments about PA scope of practice or their collaboration with physicians. The key distinction is the focus on correcting misrepresentations of PA professional status. This matters for ensuring health IT systems appropriately recognize PA roles.

description: Modification of "Base EHR" Definition for PA Inclusivity
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses specific language within the "Base EHR" definition that needs modification for inclusivity of Physician Associates (PAs). It includes recommending the amendment of "physician order entry" to "health care provider order entry" to ensure non-physician prescribers, including PAs, are appropriately included, excluding other aspects of the Base EHR definition or other provider types. The key distinction is the focus on a specific phrase within the Base EHR definition to ensure PA inclusivity. This matters for aligning health IT capabilities with the actual practice of medicine.

description: Facilitators of Reproductive Healthcare Access
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the protection and inclusion of individuals who assist patients in accessing reproductive healthcare within information blocking exceptions. It focuses on their inclusion within information blocking exceptions and ensuring healthcare providers are also protected when interacting with these facilitators, excluding general patient privacy or the provision of reproductive healthcare services themselves. The key distinction is the focus on protecting specific individuals who play a supportive role in reproductive health access. This matters for ensuring patient access and provider willingness to offer care.

description: Explicit Inclusion in Information Blocking Exceptions
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the need for explicit clarification that individuals facilitating reproductive healthcare access are protected under relevant exceptions. It includes recommendations to clearly state that facilitators such as consent providers for minors or transportation providers are covered by the exception, excluding the definition of reproductive healthcare or the protection of patients themselves. The key distinction is the focus on explicitly naming and protecting facilitators of care. This matters for ensuring support networks are not inadvertently penalized.

description: Protection for Healthcare Providers Interacting with Facilitators
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need to ensure healthcare providers are protected when their interactions involve facilitators of reproductive healthcare access. It includes seeking assurances that doctors and hospitals remain protected when working with individuals who provide consent or transportation for patients seeking reproductive health care, excluding the protection of the facilitators themselves or the patients. The key distinction is the focus on safeguarding the providers who engage with these patient support persons. This matters for enabling providers to support patient needs without undue risk.

description: Pediatric and Adolescent Patient Considerations
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the unique needs and considerations for pediatric and adolescent patients within health IT regulations, focusing on tailored requirements. It includes the development of pediatric-specific API certification criteria, addressing adolescent confidentiality, and enhancing patient access API provisions for proxy access and minor consent management, excluding general patient access or adult patient needs. The key distinction is the focus on tailoring regulations to the specific vulnerabilities and requirements of minors. This matters for ensuring patient safety and appropriate care for children.

description: Pediatric-Specific Certification Criteria for APIs
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for certification criteria tailored to the unique requirements of pediatric patients for APIs. It includes calls for developing and requiring pediatric-specific criteria for application program interfaces (APIs) to ensure HIT products meet the distinct needs of children's hospitals and families, excluding general API certification or requirements for adult patients. The key distinction is the focus on creating specialized certification standards for pediatric-focused APIs. This matters for preventing customization workarounds and ensuring interoperability for pediatric care.

description: Adolescent Confidentiality in Health Data Sharing
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the importance of maintaining adolescent confidentiality and managing sensitive health information for minors during data sharing. It includes concerns about potential risks to adolescent confidentiality if information blocking exceptions are not flexible enough and the need for specific consent mechanisms for sensitive data, excluding general patient privacy or adult confidentiality concerns. The key distinction is the focus on the specific privacy needs of adolescents, particularly regarding sensitive health information. This matters for protecting minors and encouraging them to seek necessary care.

description: Patient Access API Provisions for Proxy Access (Minors)
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers enhancements to patient access API provisions to better address pediatric and adolescent-specific issues, including parental/guardian involvement. It includes strengthening these provisions to incorporate proxy access for parents/guardians and privacy protections for managing minor access when necessary, excluding general patient access or proxy access for adults. The key distinction is the focus on tailoring patient access APIs to the complexities of minor consent and parental involvement. This matters for ensuring appropriate data access while safeguarding minors.

description: Public Health Agency Support and Transition
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the support and resources needed for public health agencies to effectively adopt new interoperability standards and modernize their systems. It includes providing realistic timelines, adequate resources, pilot implementations, and collaboration with pediatric experts for public health data modernization, excluding support for other types of healthcare entities or general policy directives. The key distinction is the focus on enabling public health agencies to meet new interoperability mandates. This matters for strengthening the nation's public health infrastructure.

description: Resources and Timelines for Public Health Agency Transition
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for realistic timelines and adequate resources to support public health agencies in their transition to new interoperability standards. It includes calls for providing sufficient time and funding for agencies to acquire, implement, and maintain certified HIT, particularly for adopting FHIR and transitioning from legacy standards, excluding the transition requirements for other healthcare entities. The key distinction is the focus on the specific needs of public health agencies for implementing new technologies. This matters because public health systems often require significant investment and lead time.

description: Pilot Implementations for New Public Health Standards
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the recommendation to conduct pilot projects and gather real-world experience before broadly incorporating new standards into public health certification. It includes advocating for pilot implementations for new standards like FHIR to ensure their practical applicability and gather necessary feedback before widespread adoption, excluding pilot programs for other sectors or general standard development. The key distinction is the focus on piloting new standards specifically for public health use cases. This matters for ensuring the successful and efficient adoption of new technologies in this critical sector.

description: Pediatric Stakeholder Consultation for Public Health Data Infrastructure
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the importance of consulting pediatric experts to inform the development of public health data infrastructure and ensure it meets child health needs. It includes recommendations for collaboration with pediatric expert stakeholders to build a national data infrastructure capable of efficiently sharing public health information, including pediatric-specific data, excluding consultation with other stakeholder groups or general data infrastructure development. The key distinction is the focus on engaging pediatric experts to ensure the infrastructure meets the needs of children. This matters for improving child health outcomes and data accessibility.

description: Cancer Surveillance Ecosystem Support
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the specific needs and support required for the cancer surveillance ecosystem, particularly central cancer registries, to meet new reporting mandates. It includes recommendations on the preferred standards for pathology reporting and the provision of resources to build and validate new data streams, excluding other public health reporting or general data standards. The key distinction is the focus on the unique needs and constraints of cancer registries. This matters for maintaining effective cancer surveillance and control programs.

description: Preference for NAACCR Volume V Standard for Cancer Pathology
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the recommendation to promote the use of the NAACCR Volume V standard for cancer pathology reporting instead of mandating the HL7® FHIR Cancer Pathology Data Sharing Implementation Guide. It includes arguments that this preference is due to the current lack of FHIR adoption by laboratories and the associated significant costs, excluding support for FHIR adoption in general or other cancer data reporting mechanisms. The key distinction is the advocacy for a specific, existing standard (NAACCR Vol V) over a newer mandated one for pathology reporting. This matters for practical implementation and cost-effectiveness in cancer data collection.

description: Resource Needs for Central Cancer Registries
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the critical need for substantial support and resources to be provided to central cancer registries for them to meet evolving reporting mandates. It includes recommendations for building, testing, and validating new data streams and workflows required by the proposed rule, while enabling them to maintain current workflows, especially given funding limitations, excluding resource needs for other public health entities or general developer support. The key distinction is the focus on the specific resource requirements of central cancer registries. This matters for their capacity to meet evolving reporting mandates.

description: Release of Information (ROI) Service Provider Concerns
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the concerns of organizations that provide Release of Information (ROI) services for patient health information, focusing on market flexibility. It includes ensuring flexibility in EPHI transmission pathways and preventing standardized API criteria from stifling competition or creating mandatory certification processes, excluding general patient access or data security requirements outside of the context of ROI services. The key distinction is the focus on the operational and competitive landscape for ROI providers. This matters for ensuring a competitive market for essential health information management services.

description: Flexibility in EPHI Transmission Pathways for ROI Providers
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for flexibility in how covered entities and business associates securely transmit electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI) for ROI services. It includes advocating for allowing secure transmission through alternative pathways, rather than solely engaging with ONC-certified technology or TEFCA participants, to foster competition and support diverse exchange methods, excluding the security requirements of ePHI transmission or general information exchange protocols. The key distinction is the focus on maintaining flexibility in exchange pathways to promote competition. This matters for ensuring that smaller ROI providers are not disadvantaged.

description: Preventing Competition Stifling via Standards for ROI Providers
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses concerns that standardized API criteria could inadvertently stifle competition within the health IT market for ROI services. It includes ensuring that such criteria do not result in mandatory certification processes, thereby preserving flexibility for entities to select technology that meets robust security and privacy standards, excluding the merits of standardization or the technical specifications of APIs. The key distinction is the focus on the potential anti-competitive effects of certification mandates. This matters for promoting a diverse and innovative health IT marketplace.

description: Patient Access, Engagement, and Trust
detailed_guidelines: This category focuses on how patients can access their health information and engage with their care through health IT, emphasizing their perspective and experience. It covers the completeness of EHI exports, the quality of patient education resources, the preservation of patient-provider trust, and the user experience for accessing data and interacting with consumer-facing applications, excluding the technical standards for data exchange or information blocking rules, except where they directly impact patient access or engagement. The key distinction is the focus on the patient's perspective and experience with health IT. This matters for empowering patients in their healthcare journey.

description: Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export Completeness
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the critical aspect of ensuring patients can access complete and comprehensive Electronic Health Information (EHI), including often-omitted historical data. It includes mandating the inclusion of historical data, specific data types often missing, and critiquing the adequacy of current export formats for capturing comprehensive information, excluding general patient access via portals or the technical standards for data exchange. The key distinction is the focus on the content and completeness of the exported EHI. This matters for enabling informed patient decision-making and care continuity.

description: Completeness of EHI Exports including Historical Data
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for EHI exports to be full and complete, including critical historical data often omitted from standard exports. It includes requirements for exports to incorporate significant historical data that is often omitted from current standard exports, highlighting missing data types like historic labs, clinical notes, and therapy records, excluding the process of exporting data or the format of exports. The key distinction is the focus on the comprehensiveness and thoroughness of the exported EHI content. This matters for ensuring patients have access to all necessary information for their care.

description: Mandated Inclusion of Specific Data Types in EHI Export
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the identification and mandate for inclusion of specific data types within EHI exports that are currently omitted, critical for managing complex conditions. It highlights the omission of essential data such as historic labs, clinical notes, and detailed records of therapies (e.g., ECMO support) from standard exports, excluding the general availability of EHI or other types of health information. The key distinction is the focus on particular data categories that are critical for managing complex health conditions. This matters because missing data can hinder diagnosis and treatment.

description: Adequacy of Current EHI Export Formats
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the critique of current EHI export formats for their ability to capture comprehensive historical information needed by patients. It includes commentary arguing that existing formats like PDFs, C-CDAs, and FHIR documents do not adequately capture the necessary historical data for diagnosing complex conditions, excluding recommendations for new formats, only the critique of existing ones. The key distinction is the assessment of whether current formats are sufficient for comprehensive data capture. This matters for ensuring patients receive usable and complete health information.

description: Patient Education Resource Standards
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the importance of patient-specific education resources within health IT certification and patient engagement strategies, ensuring health literacy. It includes objecting to the removal of the certification criterion for patient-specific education resources, advocating for its modernization with AI, and recommending regulatory codification until FHIR standards are established, excluding general patient access to EHI or information blocking. The key distinction is the focus on tailored educational materials provided through health IT. This matters for improving health literacy and patient adherence.

description: Retention of Patient-Specific Education Criterion
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the objection to the removal of the certification criterion for patient-specific education resources, fearing it will widen health disparities. It argues that eliminating this criterion could widen health disparities due to varying patient health literacy levels, impacting comprehension and adherence, excluding general patient engagement strategies or other certification criteria. The key distinction is the focus on retaining a specific criterion that supports personalized patient education. This matters for promoting health equity and effective patient self-management.

description: Modernization of Health IT Patient Education Resources
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the recommendation to update the patient-specific education resources certification criterion to incorporate new technologies like AI. It includes proposals to integrate advancements in automation and AI-driven patient education to reflect current capabilities and encourage ongoing innovation in health IT solutions, excluding the original purpose of the criterion or the elimination of other criteria. The key distinction is the focus on updating the criterion to leverage modern technological capabilities. This matters for ensuring patient education tools remain relevant and effective.

description: Regulatory Codification of Education Resources Pending FHIR Standards
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need to codify patient education resources in regulations until clear FHIR standards are established for related functionalities. It includes recommending regulatory codification until FHIR standards are aligned with the HL7 Context-Aware Knowledge Retrieval (Infobutton) standard, due to the current absence of a direct FHIR equivalent, excluding the elimination of the criterion or the development of FHIR standards independently. The key distinction is the call for immediate regulatory action to preserve educational resource standards pending FHIR development. This matters for ensuring continuity of essential patient education support.

description: Patient-Provider Trust and Data Sensitivity Management
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses how health IT impacts the trust between patients and providers, particularly concerning sensitive information and pediatric patients. It includes prioritizing patient-provider trust, especially regarding reproductive health data, and concerns about the risks of direct EHI access for pediatric patients without provider review, excluding the technical aspects of data exchange or general patient engagement. The key distinction is the focus on the relational aspect of care and the impact of health IT on that trust. This matters for fostering open communication and effective care delivery.

description: Prioritizing Patient-Provider Trust in Data Sharing
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the critical importance of maintaining and prioritizing patient-provider trust within the context of health information sharing. It includes emphasizing the delicate balance required when dealing with sensitive health information, particularly related to reproductive health, and ensuring that health IT practices do not erode this trust, excluding the specific mechanisms of data sharing or information blocking rules themselves. The key distinction is the focus on the foundational trust relationship between patients and providers. This matters for encouraging open dialogue and effective care management.

description: Risks of Direct EHI Access for Pediatric Patients Without Review
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers concerns about the potential harm to pediatric patients from immediate access to EHI via portals without provider interpretation. It includes concerns that such access could lead to distress or confusion, especially for young patients or teenagers, and could have unintended consequences for adolescent confidentiality, excluding general EHI access for adults or the benefits of patient access. The key distinction is the focus on the unique vulnerabilities of pediatric patients to direct, unmediated access to their health information. This matters for ensuring patient safety and appropriate information delivery.

description: Consumer-Facing Application Usability and Support
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the support and usability of consumer-facing applications that connect to health data, ensuring they are accessible and free from unreasonable burdens. It includes preventing "special effort" practices by developers, enhancing onboarding processes, and ensuring adherence to API conditions and maintenance of certification, excluding general patient access to EHI or the standards for the data itself. The key distinction is the focus on the experience and support provided by applications that leverage health data. This matters for enabling patients to use third-party tools effectively.

description: Preventing "Special Effort" Practices for Consumer Health Apps
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need to prevent practices that introduce undue burdens or delays for consumer-facing applications seeking to access health data. It includes announcing policy guidance and holding Certified API Developers accountable for failing to implement standards-conforming APIs or for instituting registration practices that introduce unreasonable burdens, excluding general API requirements or information blocking policies broadly. The key distinction is the focus on identifying and penalizing "special effort" that hinders consumer app functionality. This matters for fostering a seamless patient data ecosystem.

description: Streamlining Onboarding Processes for Consumer Health Apps
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the need to streamline the processes by which consumer-facing applications onboard and connect to health data systems, facilitating quicker integration. It includes addressing onboarding practices that introduce unreasonable burdens, conflict with interpretive guidance on customer approval, or effectively require patient requests for connections, potentially causing information blocking, excluding the technical connection methods or the data itself. The key distinction is the focus on the administrative and procedural aspects of application onboarding. This matters for facilitating quicker and more efficient integration of third-party apps.

description: Security, Privacy, and Authentication
detailed_guidelines: This category addresses the security and privacy measures required within health IT systems, including authentication, encryption, and handling of sensitive data. It covers Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) flexibility, server-side encryption, and specific considerations for adolescent confidentiality and reproductive health data, excluding general data exchange standards or information blocking policies, but rather the safeguards for data integrity and confidentiality. The key distinction is the focus on protecting the security and privacy of health information. This matters for building trust and preventing unauthorized access or misuse.

description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the requirements and implementation considerations for Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) in health IT to enhance access security. It includes recommendations for flexibility in MFA methods, requirements for disaster recovery and usability, and guidance on integrating MFA with legacy systems, excluding single-factor authentication or the general need for security. The key distinction is the focus on the specific implementation details and requirements for MFA. This matters for enhancing the security of access to health information.

description: Flexibility in MFA Method Choices
detailed_guidelines: This theme covers the need for flexibility in the types of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) methods supported by health IT systems. It includes ensuring support for various methods like biometrics, hardware tokens, and app-based authentication, and aligning these choices with NIST Digital Identity Guidelines, excluding the mandate for MFA itself or specific implementation standards outside of NIST. The key distinction is the focus on the variety and adaptability of MFA solutions. This matters for accommodating user preferences and technological advancements.

description: Disaster Recovery and Usability for MFA Implementations
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for robust disaster recovery plans and user-friendly implementation of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). It includes requiring disaster recovery and failover plans for MFA implementations, as well as incorporating usability standards and guidelines into MFA certification, excluding the technical implementation of MFA beyond its usability and resilience. The key distinction is the focus on the operational resilience and user experience of MFA. This matters for ensuring consistent access and mitigating disruption.

description: MFA Integration Challenges with Legacy Health IT Systems
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the challenges and guidance required for integrating Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) into existing legacy health IT systems. It includes providing clear guidance on how to adapt MFA for legacy systems that may not have native support, ensuring secure integration without compromising existing infrastructure, excluding the implementation of MFA in new systems or general security for legacy systems. The key distinction is the focus on the specific process of integrating MFA into older systems. This matters for enabling secure access across the entire health IT landscape.

description: Server-Side Encryption Standards
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses requirements related to encrypting health data at rest on servers, ensuring data confidentiality. It includes the need for clarification on the definition of "personally identifiable health information" used in server-side encryption requirements, excluding encryption in transit or general data security practices. The key distinction is the focus on the specific definition of data to be encrypted on servers. This matters for ensuring the scope of encryption mandates is clear and appropriate.

description: Clarification of PII/PHI Definition for Server-Side Encryption
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for clarity regarding the definition of "personally identifiable health information" in the context of server-side encryption requirements. It includes calls for precise definition to ensure the correct scope of data subject to encryption on servers, excluding the technical implementation of encryption or definitions of PII for other purposes. The key distinction is the focus on the precise definition of data to be encrypted on servers. This matters for ensuring compliance and appropriate data protection.

description: Sensitive Health Data and Consent Management
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the specific security and privacy considerations for handling sensitive health data, including adolescent confidentiality and reproductive health data. It covers adolescent confidentiality, the protection of reproductive health data, and the need for specific consent mechanisms tailored for minors, excluding general patient data privacy or the management of non-sensitive information. The key distinction is the focus on highly sensitive data categories and the particular challenges of managing consent for minors. This matters for protecting vulnerable populations and ensuring ethical data handling.

description: Adolescent Confidentiality in Health Data Sharing
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the critical need to maintain adolescent confidentiality when health information is shared, protecting minors' privacy. It includes concerns about the potential risks to adolescent confidentiality if information blocking exceptions are not sufficiently flexible and the need for specific consent mechanisms tailored for minors when sharing sensitive data, excluding general patient privacy or adult confidentiality. The key distinction is the focus on the specific privacy needs of adolescents, particularly concerning sensitive health information. This matters for protecting minors and encouraging them to seek necessary care.

description: Protection of Reproductive Health Data via Information Blocking Exceptions
detailed_guidelines: This theme addresses the need for specific protections for reproductive health data within information blocking regulations via tailored exceptions. It includes establishing a clear and flexible information blocking exception specifically for reproductive health information to protect patients and providers from the misuse of this data, excluding other types of sensitive data or general reproductive health policy. The key distinction is the focus on safeguarding reproductive health data specifically through an information blocking exception. This matters for ensuring access to reproductive healthcare services without fear of data misuse.
